"title": "MicroRNA-196a is regulated by ER and is a prognostic biomarker in ER+ Breast Cancer",
"authors": "Michael J G Milevskiy, Udai Gujral, Carolina Del Lama Marques, Andrew Stone, Korinne Northwood, Lez J Burke, Julia M W Gee, Kenneth Nephew, Susan Clark, Melissa A Brown",
"field_subfield": "Molecular oncology / epigenetics of microRNA regulation in breast cancer",
"type_of_paper": "Research article (bioRxiv preprint)",
"executive_summary": "This study investigates the transcriptional regulation and clinical significance of the microRNA MIR196A (miR-196a), which is encoded at two genomic loci (MIR196A2 at the HOXC locus on chromosome 12 and MIR196A1 at the HOXB locus on chromosome 17). Although miR-196a has been implicated as an oncogene in breast, lung, and other cancers, its transcriptional regulation remained poorly understood. The authors demonstrate that MIR196A expression is dynamically regulated by oestrogen through the oestrogen receptor alpha (ERα) and its cofactor FOXA1, acting via long-range enhancer-promoter interactions. Using MCF7 breast cancer cells, they show that oestrogen stimulates nascent MIR196A2 transcription, peaking 40 minutes after oestradiol addition, and that this is mediated by ERα binding to putative promoter regions (PP1 and PP3) and distal enhancers, including the previously characterised HOTAIR distal enhancer (HDE) and a novel MIR196A2-Enhancer (mE). The authors also identify that a CpG island upstream of MIR196A2, previously associated with reduced breast cancer risk, lies within the transcriptionally active region and is subject to DNA methylation regulation. Clinically, MIR196A is significantly overexpressed in breast tumours relative to normal tissue, correlates with tumour stage, and serves as a prognostic biomarker. High MIR196A expression is associated with poor survival in ER+ breast cancer, particularly in post-menopausal women and in tumours resistant to hormone therapy and chemotherapy, whereas it associates with better outcomes in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). The findings provide a mechanistic understanding of MIR196A regulation and a novel stratification method for therapeutically resistant ER+ breast cancer. The study highlights the complexity of MIR196A expression, driven by dual-locus encoding and coordinated enhancer activity, and suggests that de-repression of HOXC enhancer elements contributes to therapeutic resistance. This work contributes to the broader understanding of microRNA regulation in cancer and identifies potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for ER+ breast cancer management.",

{
"title": "MicroRNA-196a is regulated by ER and is a prognostic biomarker in ER+ Breast Cancer",
"authors": "Michael J G Milevskiy, Udai Gujral, Carolina Del Lama Marques, Andrew Stone, Korinne Northwood, Lez J Burke, Julia M W Gee, Kenneth Nephew, Susan Clark, Melissa A Brown",
"field_subfield": "Molecular oncology / microRNA regulation in breast cancer",
"type_of_paper": "Research article (bioRxiv preprint)",
"executive_summary": "MicroRNAs are potent post-transcriptional regulators involved in all hallmarks of cancer. This study focuses on MIR196A, which is transcribed from two loci and implicated in developmental and pathogenic processes, with targets including Hox, Fox, Cdk inhibitors and annexins. The authors note that genetic variants and altered expression of miR196a are associated with risk and progression of multiple cancers including breast cancer, however little is known about the regulation of the genes encoding this miRNA, nor the impact of variants therein. The central aim was to characterise the expression landscape of MIR196A including factors regulating its expression and explore potential roles of regulatory elements and factors in breast cancer prognostication. Using MCF7 cells, the authors demonstrated that MIR196A displays complex and dynamic expression patterns, in part controlled by long range transcriptional regulation between promoter and enhancer elements bound by ERα. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP-Seq) for RNA polymerase II demonstrates that polymerase binding in the region surrounding the HOXC10 gene and MIR196A gene is dependent on oestrogen in MCF7 cells and is repressed with both tamoxifen or fulvestrant treatment. Global-run-on sequencing (GRO-Seq) analysis of MCF7 cells clearly indicates a dramatic increase in RNA production in the genomic region surrounding MIR196A2, peaking at 40 mins following addition of oestradiol (E2). These data clearly indicate an increase in precursor miRNA from MIR196A2 but not MIR196A1 in response to E2. To identify the structural elements associated with the transcriptional regulation of MIR196A, histone methylation patterns in the MCF7 breast cancer cell line were assessed. Using publicly available datasets, the authors established that oestrogen mediated upregulation of miR-196A expression is accompanied by binding of ERα and its pioneer factor FOXA1 to two putative promoter regions, putative promoters 1 and 3 (PP1 and PP3), upstream of the miR196A2 transcription start site. Using ChIA-PET genome-wide chromatin interactions that immunoprecipitate with either ERα or RNA Polymerase II, the authors identified two major sites of interaction with the MIR196A2 promoters. One of these is a previously identified HOTAIR enhancer (HDE) and the other a novel interacting partner (MIR196A2-Enhancer, mE). Chromosome conformation capture (3C) and 3C-qPCR demonstrate that both enhancer elements physically interact with each of the two MIR196A2/HOXC10 promoter regions. The authors then investigated MIR196A expression patterns in relation to commonly utilised molecular markers of breast tumours, identifying four distinct clusters of MIR196A expression. Using the METABRIC cohort of breast tumours, expression analysis indicates that MIR196A is significantly over-expressed in breast tumours compared to normal adjacent tissue and over-expression is associated with an increase in tumour stage. High expression of MIR196A is associated with a poor survival in estrogen receptor positive (ER+) breast cancer, whilst high expression associates with a better outcome in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Using MIR196A expression, overall survival of ER+ tumours responding to both hormone therapy (HT) and chemotherapy (CT) was stratified. Women with low MIR196A expression had exhibited a high rate of survival (>95% at 10 years), whilst most women within the high expression group died within 17 years (61% at 10 years). The effects of menopause on the stratification of survival for ER+ women were investigated. In premenopausal women, high expression of MIR196A is associated with a good outcome in ER+ disease. Multivariate analysis demonstrates that MIR196A is one of the few significant biomarkers for ER+ tumours arising before menopause. In post-menopausal women, all tested biomarkers were significant in ER+ disease, including MIR196A, however high expression is now associated with a poor outcome. Using established models of HR+ disease resistance, the authors found that MIR196A expression is significantly increased in tamoxifen resistant MCF7 cells (TAMR) whilst it is almost depleted in fulvestrant resistance (FASR). For HR+ resistant tumours the only remaining therapeutic options are radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Using RNA-Seq data for cell line models of resistance to paclitaxel and adriamycin, two common chemotherapeutics, MIR196A expression again increases in resistant cell lines compared to the treatment sensitive cell line. Utilising ERα ChIP-Seq performed in human patients with HR+ disease, binding sites for ERα were identified in the genomic region of MIR196A. This tumour cohort contains women who respond to HR therapy, those who do not and metastases from resistant tumours. An increase in ERα occupancy is seen at both enhancer and promoter regions of MIR196A in non-responders and metastases. This work sheds light on the normal and abnormal regulation of MIR196A and provides a novel stratification method for therapeutically resistant breast cancer.",

summary.title: MicroRNA-196a is regulated by ER and is a prognostic biomarker in ER+ Breast Cancer
summary.authors: Michael J G Milevskiy, Udai Gujral, Carolina Del Lama Marques, Andrew Stone, Korinne Northwood, Lez J Burke, Julia M W Gee, Kenneth Nephew, Susan Clark, Melissa A Brown
summary.field_subfield: Molecular oncology / microRNA regulation in breast cancer
summary.executive_summary: MicroRNAs are potent post-transcriptional regulators involved in all hallmarks of cancer. This study focuses on MIR196A, which is transcribed from two loci and implicated in developmental and pathogenic processes, with targets including Hox, Fox, Cdk inhibitors and annexins. The authors note that genetic variants and altered expression of miR196a are associated with risk and progression of multiple cancers including breast cancer, however little is known about the regulation of the genes encoding this miRNA, nor the impact of variants therein. The central aim was to characterise the expression landscape of MIR196A including factors regulating its expression and explore potential roles of regulatory elements and factors in breast cancer prognostication. Using MCF7 cells, the authors demonstrated that MIR196A displays complex and dynamic expression patterns, in part controlled by long range transcriptional regulation between promoter and enhancer elements bound by ERα. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP-Seq) for RNA polymerase II demonstrates that polymerase binding in the region surrounding the HOXC10 gene and MIR196A gene is dependent on oestrogen in MCF7 cells and is repressed with both tamoxifen or fulvestrant treatment. Global-run-on sequencing (GRO-Seq) analysis of MCF7 cells clearly indicates a dramatic increase in RNA production in the genomic region surrounding MIR196A2, peaking at 40 mins following addition of oestradiol (E2). These data clearly indicate an increase in precursor miRNA from MIR196A2 but not MIR196A1 in response to E2. To identify the structural elements associated with the transcriptional regulation of MIR196A, histone methylation patterns in the MCF7 breast cancer cell line were assessed. Using publicly available datasets, the authors established that oestrogen mediated upregulation of miR-196A expression is accompanied by binding of ERα and its pioneer factor FOXA1 to two putative promoter regions, putative promoters 1 and 3 (PP1 and PP3), upstream of the miR196A2 transcription start site. Using ChIA-PET genome-wide chromatin interactions that immunoprecipitate with either ERα or RNA Polymerase II, the authors identified two major sites of interaction with the MIR196A2 promoters. One of these is a previously identified HOTAIR enhancer (HDE) and the other a novel interacting partner (MIR196A2-Enhancer, mE). Chromosome conformation capture (3C) and 3C-qPCR demonstrate that both enhancer elements physically interact with each of the two MIR196A2/HOXC10 promoter regions. The authors then investigated MIR196A expression patterns in relation to commonly utilised molecular markers of breast tumours, identifying four distinct clusters of MIR196A expression. Using the METABRIC cohort of breast tumours, expression analysis indicates that MIR196A is significantly over-expressed in breast tumours compared to normal adjacent tissue and over-expression is associated with an increase in tumour stage. High expression of MIR196A is associated with a poor survival in estrogen receptor positive (ER+) breast cancer, whilst high expression associates with a better outcome in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Using MIR196A expression, overall survival of ER+ tumours responding to both hormone therapy (HT) and chemotherapy (CT) was stratified. Women with low MIR196A expression had exhibited a high rate of survival (>95% at 10 years), whilst most women within the high expression group died within 17 years (61% at 10 years). The effects of menopause on the stratification of survival for ER+ women were investigated. In premenopausal women, high expression of MIR196A is associated with a good outcome in ER+ disease. Multivariate analysis demonstrates that MIR196A is one of the few significant biomarkers for ER+ tumours arising before menopause. In post-menopausal women, all tested biomarkers were significant in ER+ disease, including MIR196A, however high expression is now associated with a poor outcome. Using established models of HR+ disease resistance, the authors found that MIR196A expression is significantly increased in tamoxifen resistant MCF7 cells (TAMR) whilst it is almost depleted in fulvestrant resistance (FASR). For HR+ resistant tumours the only remaining therapeutic options are radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Using RNA-Seq data for cell line models of resistance to paclitaxel and adriamycin, two common chemotherapeutics, MIR196A expression again increases in resistant cell lines compared to the treatment sensitive cell line. Utilising ERα ChIP-Seq performed in human patients with HR+ disease, binding sites for ERα were identified in the genomic region of MIR196A. This tumour cohort contains women who respond to HR therapy, those who do not and metastases from resistant tumours. An increase in ERα occupancy is seen at both enhancer and promoter regions of MIR196A in non-responders and metastases. This work sheds light on the normal and abnormal regulation of MIR196A and provides a novel stratification method for therapeutically resistant breast cancer.

claims.description: MIR196A2 is transcriptionally regulated by oestrogen via ERα-bound promoter and enhancer elements.
High MIR196A expression is a prognostic biomarker of poor outcome in ER+ breast cancer, particularly in advanced and post-menopausal disease.
Therapeutic resistance leads to increases in MIR196A expression, linking its regulation to endocrine and chemotherapeutic resistance.

Research Context
MicroRNAs are potent post-transcriptional regulators involved in all hallmarks of cancer. MIR196A is transcribed from two loci and has been implicated in a wide range of developmental and pathogenic processes. MIR196A is overexpressed in breast tumours, and a SNP within the MIR196A2 gene is associated with a decreased risk of breast cancer. Despite the clear importance on miR-196a in cancer, its transcriptional regulation remains poorly understood. Several instances of miRNA regulation by enhancers have been described, but this area is very much in its infancy. The expression of MIR196A in breast cancer is both dynamic and complex. This work sheds light on the normal and abnormal regulation of MIR196A and provides a novel stratification method for therapeutically resistant breast cancer.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aimed to characterise the expression landscape of MIR196A including factors regulating its expression and explore potential roles of regulatory elements and factors in breast cancer prognostication. Given that MIR196A expression strongly correlates with expression of HOXC protein coding genes in breast cancer, the authors sought to determine if oestrogen also regulates MIR196A2. Given that MIR196A expression is regulated by oestrogen we hypothesized that its transcription may be controlled by the oestrogen receptor (ER). Given that ERα often binds to distal enhancer elements to exert its function, we examined the hypothesis that MIR196A2 is controlled by long-range transcriptional regulation, mediated by ERα tethered gene looping. Given that MIR196A is regulated by ERα, we investigated its expression patterns in relation to commonly utilised molecular markers of breast tumours. High expression of MIR196A is a biomarker of poor prognosis in ER+ tumours, especially in those patients resistant to therapy. We hypothesise that a consorted effort of multiple enhancers is responsible for the overexpression of these genes in cancer possibly driven by extensive binding and activity of ERα. Future studies should aim to uncover the purpose of increase MIR196A expression and if it is required for development of resistance alone or in combination with other HOXC genes.

Methodological Details
MCF7 cells, for the development of endocrine resistance sub-lines, were obtained from AstraZeneca. MCF7, Tamoxifen-resistant (TAMR), Fulvestrant-resistant (FASR), and oestrogen-deprived (MCF7x) cells were cultured as described. All cell lines were cultured for less than 6 months after authentication by short-tandem repeat (STR) profiling. MCF7 cells were transfected with 500 ng of modified pGL3 reporter constructs, 20 ng of pRL-TK and 0.5μL of Lipofectamine 3000. 48 hours post transfection luciferase readings were measured using a DTX-880 luminometer and Dual-Glo Stop and Glo luciferase reporter kit. Cell lysates were prepared using Life Technologies TRIzol reagent and RNA was chloroform extracted and isopropanol precipitated. RNA for miRNA analysis was reverse transcribed using the miScript RT II kit from Qiagen. Assays for all miRNAs were performed with Qiagen's miScript SYBR Green PCR Kit. Expression data for miRNAs was normalised to the snoRNA RNU6b. All qRT-PCRs were performed using the protocols advised by the manufacturers on a Corbet Rotorgene-6000. RNA-Seq on MCF7 cells following oestradiol treatment was performed as described previously by K. Nephew. RNA-Seq from Adriamycin (ADM) and paclitaxel (PTX) resistant MCF7 derived cells was sourced from GSE68815. Expression of HOX genes in human breast cells was sourced from Gascard et al. Accession codes for publically available data were MCF7 ChIP-Seq (GSE14664), GRO-Seq (GSE27463), ChIA-PET (GSE39495), Breast tumour ERα ChIP-Seq (GSE32222). MCF7 histone ChIP-Seq and breast cell 450K array data was sourced from ENCODE via http://genome.ucsc.edu/ENCODE/downloads.html. ChIP-Seq data was mapped with Bowtie and peaks called by MACS and viewed in the Interactive Genome Viewer (IGV). DNA methylation of breast tumours was sourced from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and correlated to the gene expression of MIR196A from the TCGA cohort. METABRIC expression and clinical information were sourced from EGAS00000083. Clustering of Illumina Array and miR-Seq data was performed using the Multiple Experiment Viewer (MeV). Data was mean-centred and hierarchically clustered via Manhattan average-linkage based clustering of both rows and columns. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazard regression analyses were performed using MedCalc for Windows, version 12.7. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and generation of survival curves was done GraphPad Prism. Optimal cutoffs for low and high expression groups were determined using receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curves. Chromosome conformation capture (3C) was adapted from Vakoc 2005, Hagege 2007 and Tan-Wong 2008. Cells were grown to 60-80% confluence and fixed with 1% formaldehyde. Libraries were generated for each cell line using HindIII with control libraries undigested and unligated. GAPDH primers were used to determine the digestion and ligation efficiency of each library. The sample sizes for the cell culture experiments and the specific patient cohort demographics are not reported in the text.

Procedures And Architectures
All PCR products for luciferase reporter assays were ligated into Invitrogen's pCR-Blunt plasmid using T4 DNA Ligase, at 4 0 C overnight. MIR196A enhancers and promoters were digested from pCR-Blunt and cloned into the luciferase reporter plasmid pGL3-Basic. Enhancers were cloned into the BamHI/SalI site whilst promoters were cloned into the multiple cloning site immediately upstream of the luciferase gene. See Supplementary Table1 for primers. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP-Seq) for RNA polymerase II demonstrates that polymerase binding in the region surrounding the HOXC10 gene and MIR196A gene is dependent on oestrogen in MCF7 cells and is repressed with both tamoxifen or fulvestrant treatment. Global-run-on sequencing (GRO-Seq) is able to measure nascent RNA, assessing changes in transcription with high sensitivity. Analysis of MCF7 GRO-Seq data clearly indicates a dramatic increase in RNA production in the genomic region surrounding MIR196A2, peaking at 40 mins following addition of oestradiol (E2). This increase in RNA production from the HOXC locus was validated with qRT-PCR and RNA-Seq from MCF7 cells following addition of E2. This analysis uncovered putative promoter elements upstream of MIR196A including a shared promoter with HOXC10. Using publically available datasets we established that oestrogen mediated upregulation of miR-196A expression is accompanied by binding of ERα and its pioneer factor FOXA1 to two putative promoter regions, putative promoters 1 and 3 (PP1 and PP3). Upon cloning of these putative promoter sites into luciferase reporter vectors where PP1 and also PP2; modestly; increases luciferase gene transcription. we examined the hypothesis that MIR196A2 is controlled by long-range transcriptional regulation, mediated by ERα tethered gene looping. Using ChIA-PET genome-wide chromatin interactions that immunoprecipitate with either ERα or RNA Polymerase II, we identified two major sites of interaction with the MIR196A2 promoters. Chromosome conformation capture (3C) digestion of the HOXC genomic locus digests the MIR196A2 region into two fragments. 3C-qPCR demonstrates that both enhancer elements physically interact with each of the two MIR196A2/HOXC10 promoter region. Cloning of these fragments downstream of the putative promoter luciferase reporters clearly demonstrates significant augmentation of transcription for both the PP1 and PP2. Analysis of DNA methylation reveals that this CpG island is mostly methylated in non-malignant MCF10A and cancerous MCF7 cells, whilst unmethylated in human mammary epithelial cells (HMEC). Using established models of HR+ disease resistance we found that MIR196A expression is significantly increased in tamoxifen resistant MCF7 cells (TAMR) whilst it is almost depleted in fulvestrant resistance (FASR). These expression patterns match changes in DNA methylation to the HOXC10/MIR196A2 promoters in these same cells. Using RNA-Seq data for cell line models of resistance to paclitaxel and adriamycin, two common chemotherapeutics, MIR196A expression again increases in resistant cell lines compared to the treatment sensitive cell line. Utilising ERα ChIP-Seq performed in human patients with HR+ disease, binding sites for ERα were identified in the genomic region of MIR196A. This tumour cohort contains women who respond to HR therapy, those who do not and metastases from resistant tumours. An increase in ERα occupancy is seen at both enhancer and promoter regions of MIR196A in non-responders and metastases. To explore this hypothesis a high resolution chromatin interaction analysis of this region in breast cancer cells would be required, such as 5C or NG Capture-C, coupled with ERα ChIP-Seq and ChIA-PET.

Key Results
MIR196A expression highly correlates to HOXC genes, particularly HOXC10. The association between MIR196A expression and HOXC genes is more limited, observed most strongly with HOXC11 and HOXC10, the genes surrounding the MIR196A gene. MIR196A appears to be mostly expressed within the basal stem-cell (BSC) derived cells, whilst much lower in expression of the more differentiated cell types. ChIP-Seq for RNA polymerase II demonstrates that polymerase binding in the region surrounding the HOXC10 gene and MIR196A gene is dependent on oestrogen in MCF7 cells and is repressed with both tamoxifen or fulvestrant treatment. Analysis of MCF7 GRO-Seq data clearly indicates a dramatic increase in RNA production in the genomic region surrounding MIR196A2, peaking at 40 mins following addition of oestradiol (E2). This increase in RNA production from the HOXC locus was validated with qRT-PCR and RNA-Seq from MCF7 cells following addition of E2. These data clearly indicate an increase in precursor miRNA from MIR196A2 but not MIR196A1 in response to E2. This analysis uncovered putative promoter elements upstream of MIR196A including a shared promoter with HOXC10. Using publically available datasets we established that oestrogen mediated upregulation of miR-196A expression is accompanied by binding of ERα and its pioneer factor FOXA1 to two putative promoter regions, putative promoters 1 and 3 (PP1 and PP3). Upon cloning of these putative promoter sites into luciferase reporter vectors where PP1 and also PP2; modestly; increases luciferase gene transcription. Using ChIA-PET genome-wide chromatin interactions that immunoprecipitate with either ERα or RNA Polymerase II, we identified two major sites of interaction with the MIR196A2 promoters. One of these is a previously identified HOTAIR enhancer (HDE) and the other a novel interacting partner (MIR196A2-Enhancer, mE). 3C-qPCR demonstrates that both enhancer elements physically interact with each of the two MIR196A2/HOXC10 promoter region. Cloning of these fragments downstream of the putative promoter luciferase reporters clearly demonstrates significant augmentation of transcription for both the PP1 and PP2. Analysis of DNA methylation reveals that this CpG island is mostly methylated in non-malignant MCF10A and cancerous MCF7 cells, whilst unmethylated in human mammary epithelial cells (HMEC). This analysis identified four distinct clusters of MIR196A expression (Clusters 1-4). Interestingly clusters 1 and 3 show a strong correlation to expression of hormone receptors (HR) and HR cofactors. In contrast, clusters 2 and 4 have significant negative correlation to expression of ERα, PGR, FOXA1 and GATA3, whilst associating with EGFR and HER2. This expression is further defined by the PAM50 intrinsic subtypes where MIR196A is strongly expressed in the HER2 subtype. Expression analysis of this miRNA indicate that it is significantly over-expressed in breast tumours compared to normal adjacent tissue and over-expression is associated with an increase in tumour stage. High expression of MIR196A is associated with a poor survival in estrogen receptor positive (ER+) breast cancer, whilst high expression associates with a better outcome in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Women with low MIR196A expression had exhibited a high rate of survival (>95% at 10 years), whilst most women within the high expression group died within 17 years (61% at 10 years). In premenopausal women, high expression of MIR196A is associated with a good outcome in ER+ disease. Multivariate analysis demonstrates that MIR196A is one of the few significant biomarkers for ER+ tumours arising before menopause. In post-menopausal women, all tested biomarkers were significant in ER+ disease, including MIR196A, however high expression is now associated with a poor outcome. Using established models of HR+ disease resistance we found that MIR196A expression is significantly increased in tamoxifen resistant MCF7 cells (TAMR) whilst it is almost depleted in fulvestrant resistance (FASR). Using RNA-Seq data for cell line models of resistance to paclitaxel and adriamycin, two common chemotherapeutics, MIR196A expression again increases in resistant cell lines compared to the treatment sensitive cell line. An increase in ERα occupancy is seen at both enhancer and promoter regions of MIR196A in non-responders and metastases.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The authors hypothesise that a consorted effort of multiple enhancers is responsible for the overexpression of these genes in cancer possibly driven by extensive binding and activity of ERα. Given the strong correlation in expression of all HOXC genes in breast tumours with MIR196A is in stark contrast to expression in normal tissues. Interestingly, DNA methylation at several sites within the HOXC locus negatively correlates with the expression of this miRNA, supporting the notion of DNA methylation as a repressive epigenetic modification in this context. High expression of MIR196A is a biomarker of poor prognosis in ER+ tumours, especially in those patients resistant to therapy. These data raise the possibility that the pathway to resistance to therapy in ER+ tumours involves the de-repression and over-activation of promoter and enhancer elements. Given the strong involvement of HOX genes in development, we hypothesise that there is a change in the regulation and expression of these genes through and following menopause. This miRNA is a possible biomarker for the progression of breast tumour to becoming resistant to therapy. Future studies should aim to uncover the purpose of increase MIR196A expression and if it is required for development of resistance alone or in combination with other HOXC genes.

Contradictions And Limitations
The authors note that whilst we show that PP3 is not able to increase luciferase expression in a luciferase reporter assay, the binding of ERα may be important for the activity of the HOXC10 and MIR196A2 promoters. The association between MIR196A and HOXC genes is not significant in the cell types of the human breast. To explore this hypothesis a high resolution chromatin interaction analysis of this region in breast cancer cells would be required, such as 5C or NG Capture-C, coupled with ERα ChIP-Seq and ChIA-PET. It is currently unclear how dual-encoded miRs are regulated of which many exist.
